claim: Capabilities and propensities are dispositional properties, characterized by counterfactual relationships between contextual conditions and behavioural outputs, and are routinely conflated with observed performance.
stance_target: F: measurement-science framing of AI evaluation exists at the conceptual level
scope_conditions: Conceptual paper, philosophy of measurement; Feb 2026
quoted_support: We argue that capabilities and propensities are dispositional properties —stable features of systems characterised by counterfactual relationships between contextual conditions and behavioural outputs.

claim: Measuring a disposition requires (i) hypothesising causally relevant contextual properties, (ii) independently operationalising and measuring them, and (iii) empirically mapping how variation in them affects the probability of the behaviour; benchmark averages and latent-variable models like IRT bypass these steps.
stance_target: F: three-step measurement recipe, a direct framing occupant for AI evaluation (not calibration of confidence)
quoted_support: Measuring a disposition requires (i) hypothesising which contextual properties are causally relevant, (ii) independently operationalising and measuring those properties, and (iii) empirically mapping how variation in those properties affects the probability of the behaviour.

scope_conditions: Sec 1/Conclusion; ref Tal (2017) Calibration: modelling the measurement process
quoted_support: The contrast is similar to the shift from pre-scientific temperature judgements—touching an object to feel whether it is warm—to the invention of calibrated thermometers.
